svg.text: Audio Chains — RX, TX and the recording tap (SDD V2.46)
USB audio capture (per-backend device rate + name hints):
Yaesu FT-710 + the four Yaesu models — 44.1 kHz mono (the Yaesu profiles assume the family value, hw-verify) → 882-sample chunks → audio_resample 882→960
Icom IC-7300/MK2 + the three Icom models — 48 kHz native (960-sample chunks), no resample
→ Opus encode 64 kbps 20 ms (libopus ctypes) → /WSaudioRX tagged frames (PCM fallback tag) → browser AudioWorklet jitter buffer → speakers
full-duplex codecs are reopened on every TX→RX transition (restart_rx); on a failed stream open PortAudio is re-initialised once and the device is re-resolved by name (USB re-enumeration)
RX PCM (device domain) and decoded TX PCM are both tapped server-side and placed on ONE monotonic timeline (re-anchor on source switch, 50 ms continuity tolerance, real gaps filled with silence)
→ _StreamingDecimator (96-tap FIR 48k→16k) → 16 kHz mono → incremental lameenc MP3 → <freq>kHz_<date>_<time>.mp3 + recordings.json index
16 kHz is a write-only storage domain: nothing re-enters the audio path; one writer per session, dedicated thread pool, session cap MRRC_RECORDINGS_MAX_SESSION_MIN (240 min, 0 = unlimited)
getUserMedia mic → tx_capture_worklet (48 kHz mono, 960-sample frames) → tx_opus_worker (Opus 64 kbps CBR, cpx=5) → /WSaudioTX tagged frames
→ server Opus decode → 48 kHz PCM → (44.1 kHz devices only) audio_resample 960→882 → PyAudio playback → radio USB audio
PTT ownership follows the control session: the TX uplink is owned by the PTT client, same-session replacements take it over, the dead-man switch drops the carrier when that client disappears (SDD 15)
